caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1762 of 2009
lawyer:
Mahbubey Alam, Senior Advocate with (J. N. Deb, Advocate), instructed by Chowdhury Md. Zahangir -Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners 
For Respondents ------ Not represented
parties:
Md. Masuk Miah and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Md. Foyzur Rahman and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J: This petition for leave to appeal. is directed against the judgment and order dated 02.06.2009 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 5472 of 2003 discharging the. Rule and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 30.06.2003 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 3rd Court, Sylhet in Title Appeal No. 122 of 2000 affirming those dated 29.05.1999 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), First Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 67 of 1999 decreeing the suit. 

 5. Upon hearing 8 (eight) witnesses in support of the plaintiffs' case and 6 (six) witnesses in support of the defendant No.  1's case and after considering the oral and documentary evidence, the trial Court decreed the suit by judgment and order dated 29.05.2000 on the ground that the plaintiffs were able to prove that Saifullah transferred 1534.acre of land in favour of the plaintiffs; exhibit 6 series indicated that defendant No. 1 and his son Masuk Miah were witnesses of the said kabala and as such they had no title over the suit land and all the defendants' witnesses stated in their deposition that the suit second schedule land is a pathway and as such the defendants have no title or interest over the suit land. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendant Nos. 1-5, as appellants, preferred Title Appeal No. 122 of 2000 which was dismissed by judgment and decree dated 30.06.2003 mainly on the reasoning that defendant No. 1 and his son Masuk Miah were the witnesses in the said kabalas (Exhibit-6 series) and as such they had no title or interest over the suit land. 

 7. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree of the appellate Court the defendant-petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 5472 of 2003 before the High Court Division which by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule finding that Saifullah remained owner of only .09 acre of land and as such he could not transfer 1534 acre of land. Hence, the petitioners have filed the instant Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal before this Division. 

 III. Because, the vendor of the plaintiffs after exhausting his land in favour of different persons including the defendant No. 1 remained owner of only .09 acre of land and, therefore, could not sell .1534 acre of land in favour of the plaintiffs which disunities them from getting the decree as prayed for".
